summary: SundialHealth: partial conversation fragmentation, duplicate followups and rollback action plan
description:
Issue summary:
- On 2025-11-12 09:03 UTC SundialHealth began seeing partial conversation responses: first chunk delivered, subsequent chunks truncated or duplicated across parallel streams. Some sessions produced duplicate follow-ups (same assistant message sent twice) and others showed missing closing tokens causing downstream truncation in customer UI.

Impact:
- Affected ~4% of requests from SundialHealth between 09:03 and 10:24 UTC.
- High business impact: clinical note-generation workflows failed reconciliation checks; SundialHealth reported patient-facing delays and raised an executive escalation.

Environment:
- Production (us-west). Requests routed to Dedicated pool (dedicated-gpu-pool-12). Models: redwood-open-34b-v1 (primary), redwood-open-8b-quantized (fallback).

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Replay customer session trace ID sundial:20251112:09:17:34 with streaming=true, chunk_size=4096.
2) Observe first event with tokens stream, then duplicate chunk with identical token ids on second websocket connection.
3) Repeat under high concurrency (~250 rps) to reproduce amplification.

Observed behavior:
- Streaming proxy forwarded the same chunk twice to the client in ~0.8% of total streams and dropped final termination event in ~3.2% of sessions.
- Router logs show rapid rebinds for affinity keys X-Session-ID in a 30s window.

Expected behavior:
- Each session should see a single ordered stream of token chunks; termination event should arrive once per completion.

Attachments/logs:
- Link to request traces and CloudWatch dashboards in comments and confluence page.
comments: 2025-11-12 09:21 — Alex Chen: Customer opened with urgent SLA-impacting complaint. Verified streaming duplications in sample trace. Escalated to SRE. Notified account team and AMs. Opened INC-2025-11-12-01.

2025-11-12 09:45 — SRE (Jordan Patel): Initial hypothesis: streaming-proxy/broker replay loop when backend reconnection occurs during KV cache warmup. Spun up additional traces and retention of per-session socket state.

2025-11-12 10:05 — Eng (Priya Nair): Observed router rebind spikes tied to leader election events in serving-runtime; coincident with quantized fallback activation. Added feature-flagged patch to disable eager reconnection on affinity mismatch and started canary.

2025-11-12 10:28 — Support (Mei Alvarez): Notified customer of mitigation attempt: temporarily pinned traffic to primary model and disabled quantized fallback for SundialHealth. Customer confirmed reduced duplicates but reported two remaining truncated sessions.

2025-11-12 11:10 — Eng (Priya Nair): Deployed coordinated rollback of recent streaming-proxy change (PR 4682) that altered session rebind semantics; monitoring shows duplicates dropped from ~0.8% -> 0.02% and truncations resolved.
2025-11-12 13:00 — CX (Rohan Gupta): Sent incident status update to SundialHealth execs; offered 30% bill credit for impacted hour window and arranged a technical deep-dive on Nov 14.
2025-11-18 09:00 — Priya Nair: Ticket updated with root cause and next steps after post-incident review. Marking as resolved with follow-ups assigned.
2025-11-18 09:12 — SundialHealth (Elena Morales): Confirmed customer satisfied with mitigation and requested timeline for permanent fix and improved preflight checks on canary rollouts.
investigation_notes:
Timeline and findings:
- 09:03 UTC: error rate spike in streaming-proxy logs for pool dedicated-gpu-pool-12.
- 09:04-09:30 UTC: multiple leader-election events in serving-runtime coincident with autoscaler rebinds; router initiated reconnection logic that re-emitted pending chunk messages when backend ack state was missing.
- 09:15 UTC: quantized fallback was triggered due to a scheduled capacity shift; fallback handler had slightly different session-ack semantics and did not clear inflight chunk marker, enabling duplicate emission on reconnection.
- Traces: repeated token block IDs (trace evidence) and websocket closure_without_termination events.
- Reproducible locally by forcing router reconnection during inflight streaming and toggling fallback.
Hypotheses validated:
1) Combination of leader-election-induced reconnection + mismatch in fallback session-ack semantics produced duplicate chunk replay and occasional missing terminal event.
2) Canary for streaming-proxy change (PR 4682) increased sensitivity to rebind events and surfaced long-tail condition.
resolution_notes:
Immediate actions performed:
- Rolled back streaming-proxy change (PR 4682) cluster-wide at 10:05 UTC.
- Temporarily disabled model-fallback for SundialHealth and pinned requests to primary model until fix validated.
- Added rate-limit backoff on router reconnection path to avoid immediate replay of inflight chunks.
- Issued customer communication and credit proposal.
Deployment/fix status:
- Hotfix deployed 2025-11-13: harmonized session-ack semantics between primary and fallback handlers and added an idempotency guard for chunk emission.
- Regression tests added to CI for simulated reconnection flows.
- Monitoring alerts tightened to detect duplicate chunk IDs and missing termination events.
root_cause: A timing/regression issue caused by the intersection of a streaming-proxy change (PR 4682) that altered reconnection semantics and differing session-ack handling between primary and quantized fallback model handlers. Leader election/autoscaler rebind events triggered immediate reconnections which allowed inflight chunks to be emitted twice and, in some cases, prevented terminal events from being delivered.
next_steps:
1) Engineering: complete full patch rollout to all pools and run a 72-hour observation window (owner: Priya Nair).
2) QA: extend CI reconnection scenario coverage and add fuzzing for websocket disconnect/rewind (owner: QA team).
3) Product/Support: schedule a technical postmortem with SundialHealth on 2025-11-14 and finalize credit in billing system (owner: Rohan Gupta).
4) Ops: add synthetic streaming checks in us-west to detect duplicate chunk ID rate > 0.05% (owner: Jordan Patel).
5) Release: document change-control checklist for streaming-proxy rollouts to require canary traffic > 24h for reconnection-sensitive patches.
customer_impact_summary:
- Duration: ~1h20m (09:03 - 10:24 UTC) with residual degraded behavior until rollback at 10:05 but validation continued until 11:30.
- Percent of customer requests affected: ~4% peak, total impacted sessions ~1.9k.
- Business impact: clinical reconciliation jobs delayed; customer engaged exec-level escalation.
- Remediation: rollback + hotfix, customer accepted credit and scheduled PD session.
